column1: # boru Language Specification: Control flow (if do for while guard)
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# Branch/body arguments are unevaluated code lists (NoEvalArgs): `if`
# runs exactly one branch, `do` runs a body as a sub-program, `for`
# repeats a body. `guard` is the short-circuit value gate (infix form).
# §1  if cond then else — runs exactly one branch
if true [1] [2]
column3: true → then branch

column1: if false [1] [2]
column3: false → else branch

column1: if (5 gt 3) ['yes'] ['no']
column3: computed condition

column1: if true [1]
column3: two-arg form (no else) runs then when true

column1: def f fn [[b:Boolean] [Any] [ if b [99] [None] ]] f true
column3: value-or-None branch inside a fn body: then arm (checker must not halt on the None arm)

column1: def f fn [[b:Boolean] [Any] [ if b [99] [None] ]] f false
column3: value-or-None branch inside a fn body: None arm returned faithfully

column1: def f fn [[b:Boolean] [Any] [ if b [None] [None] ]] f true
column3: both-None arms in a fn body join to a plain None

column1: # §2  do — run a body as a sub-program, leaving its results
do [1 add 2]
column3: evaluates the body
all body results remain on the stack

column1: def x 5  do [x 1 add 2]
column3: a multi-value body mixing a binding read and a computed result compiles as one closure

column1: do [1 add 2 10 mul 4]
column3: an out-of-order residual (result above a literal) promotes to frame locals and re-pushes in order

column1: do [(1 add 2) (3 mul 4)]
column3: two computed results both remain, in order
a downstream word consumes the top of the multi-value residual

column1: def b true  do [1 2 (if b [] [9 9])]
column3: a variadic multi-out body (arm counts differ) compiles via the dyn-body backstop; the runtime residual lands whole

column1: do [for 3 [1] 7]
column3: a loop inside a do body compiles (the unrolled model's repeated result identities de-collide)

column1: def i 0  def ops [quote [1 add 2]]  do (ops get (i add 0))
column3: a gradual List-vs-Map operand poly re-matches at run time

column1: def f fn [[y:Integer] [Any] [do [args]]]  f 7
column3: an args-reading body compiles under the DynEnv args bracket

column1: # §3  for count body — repeat a body N times
for 3 ['x']
column3: the body runs three times

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Any] [ for n [ 5 drop ] 0 ]] f 3
column3: a carrier-count side-effect loop (body nets 0) leaves nothing; the trailing 0 is the sole return (no false "got 2")

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Any] [ for [0 n 65536] [ 5 drop ] 0 ]] f 3
column3: a computed-END range (const start/step) lowers to FOR_SETUP with a resolved end — mini-s3's s3-send-resp shape

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Any] [ for [n] [ 5 drop ] 0 ]] f 3
column3: 1-element range [end] → [0, end, 1]; a computed end still lowers

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Any] [ for [2 n] [ 5 drop ] 0 ]] f 5
column3: 2-element range [start end] with a literal start and a computed end lowers

column1: # §4  guard — `cond guard value` → value if cond else None
true guard 42
column3: passes the value when the condition holds

column1: false guard 42
column3: yields None when the condition fails

column1: # §5  truthiness — if coerces its condition

column3: non-zero is truthy → then

column1: if none [1] [2]
column3: None is falsy → else

column1: if "false" [1] [2]
column3: a non-empty string is truthy — even "false" (no magic-token falsy case, WAT §E)

column1: if "FALSE" [1] [2]
column3: likewise "FALSE" — string content is never inspected
the empty string is the only falsy string

column1: # §6  statement-boundary commit — an else-less `if` whose args arrived
# via evaluation (a paren condition) fires when the NEXT function word
# begins its own dispatch, instead of waiting to swallow that
# statement's result as a phantom else. A guard therefore raises
# BEFORE a following def's body can run (the bloom-filter report #1),
# and a value-producing statement after the guard keeps its result.
def n 0 if (n eq 0) [99] add 1 2
column3: guard fires at the barrier; add's result is not swallowed as the else

column1: def n 5 if (n eq 0) [99] add 1 2
column3: false guard: then-branch skipped, the next statement still runs

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [ if (n eq 0) [raise "zero"] def q (10 div n) q ]] f 0
column3: the guard's raise pre-empts the def body's division by zero

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [ if (n eq 0) [raise "zero"] def q (10 div n) q ]] f 5
column3: the unguarded path still computes through the def

column1: def n 0 if (n eq 0) [99] def q 1 q
column3: a following def runs AFTER the guard, not before

column1: # a parenthesised expression is NOT a barrier — it still arrives as the else

column3: paren else collected; true discards it
paren else collected; false yields it

column1: # the mirror: a parenthesised THEN expression is collected as a value too —
# true yields it, false discards it for the (value or paren) else
if (1 eq 1) (add 1 2) 88
column3: paren then collected; true yields it

column1: if (1 eq 2) (add 1 2) 88
column3: paren then collected; false yields the value else

column1: if (1 eq 1) (add 1 2) [sub 10 1]
column3: paren then; true yields it over a body else

column1: if (1 eq 2) (add 1 2) [sub 10 1]
column3: paren then discarded; false runs the body else

column1: # a computed arm also composes with a list-form condition body, lowered inline
if [1 eq 1] (add 1 2) 88
column3: list-form cond; true yields the paren then

column1: if [1 eq 2] (add 1 2) 88
column3: list-form cond; false yields the value else

column1: if [1 eq 1] 99 (add 1 2)
column3: list-form cond; true yields the value then

column1: if [1 eq 2] 99 (add 1 2)
column3: list-form cond; false yields the paren else

column1: # BOTH arms computed: both parens run eagerly (faithful), the branch selects one
if (1 eq 1) (add 1 2) (sub 9 4)
column3: both-computed; true selects the then paren

column1: if (1 eq 2) (add 1 2) (sub 9 4)
column3: both-computed; false selects the else paren

column1: add 10 (if (1 eq 1) (add 1 2) (sub 9 4))
column3: both-computed result consumed downstream

column1: # …and the statement-boundary commit composes with the core definition
# idiom: a def-fn AFTER the guard still defines (fn's speculative fill
# is untouched — the smaller-arity probe fails for def, so it waits for
# fn's result as always).
def n 0 if (n eq 0) [99] def sq fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [mul x x]] sq 5
column3: guard fires first, then the def-fn idiom proceeds

column1: def n 5 if (n eq 0) [99] def sq fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [mul x x]] sq 5
column3: false guard: definition and call unaffected

column1: # §7  while cond body — repeat a body while the condition's LAST value is truthy
# The condition region re-evaluates before every iteration and its last
# value decides (a truthiness read, not Boolean-only); body values
# accumulate onto the stack as for's do; break ends the loop with the
# values collected so far and continue abandons the current round; a def
# the body rebinds persists after the loop. Compiled on the counted
# loop's frame since the thirty-seventh increment (2026-09-09): the
# condition fragment lowers at the head of every iteration and a falsy
# value exits through FLOW_BREAK. The first four rows were
# lang/spec/frontier/frontier-while.tsv's, and the empty-condition row
# below is the fifth (the forty-second increment, 2026-09-10): a
# statically-empty condition can never produce a value, so the compiled
# program raises the interpreter's own error through a terminal trap
# instead of refusing.
while [false] ['x'] end 'done'
column3: a falsy condition runs the body zero times

column1: while [true] [break] end 'ended'
column3: break ends the loop with the values collected so far

column1: while ['ok'] [break] end 'truthy'
column3: the condition is a truthiness read, not Boolean-only

column1: def c (flex {n:0}) end while [(c get 'n') lt 3] [ (c get 'n') set 'n' ((c get 'n') add 1) c ]
column3: the classic counter loop: three iterations accumulate

column1: def n 0 end while [n lt 3] [def n (n add 1) n] end 'z'
column3: a def the body rebinds is read by the condition; body values accumulate

column1: def n 0 end while [n lt 3] [def n (n add 1)] end n
column3: a carried rebind persists after the loop

column1: def n 5 end while [n lt 3] [def n (n add 1)] end n
column3: zero iterations leave the pre-loop value

column1: while [true] [1 break] end 'x'
column3: break discards the current round's values

column1: def n 0 end while [n lt 3] [def n (n add 1) 1 continue 2] end 'z'
column3: continue discards the current round's values

column1: def n 0 end while [n lt 3] [def n (n add 1) if (n eq 2) [continue] end n] end 'z'
column3: a continue inside a branch arm skips that round's tail

column1: def n 0 end while [n lt 3] [def n (n add 1) if (n eq 2) [break] end n] end 'z'
column3: a break inside a branch arm ends the loop

column1: def f fn [[k:Integer][Integer][def n 0 while [n lt k] [def n (n add 1)] n]] end (f 4)
column3: a while inside a fn body counts against a param

column1: def n 0 end while [n lt 2] [def n (n add 1) while [true] [1 break]] end 'z'
column3: a nested while's break ends only the inner loop

column1: while [] [1]
column3: an empty condition region has no tokens, so the first round nets nothing and raises
